title: Doorbell Means Place — activity cover
note:
Cover, and the geometry is settled rather than guessed. This activity's cover used to be door-place-03-send, which failed the 16:7 Today band three times running — sliced across the eyes, then decapitated at the shoulders — because the band keeps 58% of the height and a standing adult above a floor-level bed does not fit in it. Every cover that passed first time has a crouching or kneeling human. Mirrored left-to-right against the Stay pictures on purpose: door-place-cover and door-stay-cover sit side by side on the program map rail, and a previous attempt passed every crop and still failed because at 56px the two were the same picture.

The crop instruction was rewritten from a safe area to a drawn size before the first restyle round. Stating a safe area — 'inside the middle 60% of the height' — has now failed on door-sound-03-name-distant, door-stay-03-handle, door-sound-cover and door-stay-cover; restating the same constraint as a size plus an empty margin landed first try on three of those four. A figure told to be smaller gets smaller; a figure told to stay inside a band gets moved. Re-declared for cool-flat-v2 (the plaster wall) on 2026-09-04; 2 mention(s) of the old room moved to the new hexes and wording. Round 113 under v2 came back with the figures in the lower half of the frame — the handler's head at 40% down against the clause's quarter — small in the square and smaller at 84px. The scene text now states the framing as an override, because the room description alone pulled the camera back.
scene: Interior entry hall, side view at standing eye level. MIRROR the layout used elsewhere in this program: the bed sits on the RIGHT of the frame and the closed charcoal front door on the LEFT, well away in the background. Lucy lies settled on her cool-grey dog bed — a proper mattress with real thickness, a padded slab about a hand deep with a soft raised edge, not a flat mat or a thin rug on the right — elbows and hips down, head up and level, calm and unhurried. The handler CROUCHES beside her on the bed's right, down on her heels so her head is low and near Lucy's, turned toward her, one hand resting lightly on Lucy's shoulder. She is crouching, not standing and not bending from the waist. Nothing is being offered: both her hands are empty, there is no treat anywhere in the picture. They are plainly well back from the door, with a long stretch of empty floor between them and it. No leash. HOW BIG THE PAIR IS DRAWN, which is what this cover keeps failing on: draw them SMALLER than the composition wants. The top of the crouching handler's head sits about a QUARTER of the way down from the top edge and no higher; the lowest thing that matters — the base of the bed and her feet — no lower than three quarters of the way down. Above both heads leave a clear band of empty plaster wall at least a fifth of the picture's height with nothing in it, and below them clear empty floor. Left and right, nothing that matters enters the outer eighth of the width. The app crops this two ways at once — a wide Today band that keeps only the middle strip of the HEIGHT, and a centred square that keeps only the middle three-quarters of the WIDTH — so a head near the top edge is decapitated on the app's largest surface. Empty wall above them is better than a sliced head. Take only the bed's shape, depth and cool grey from the second reference, not its open door or its guest. Background: the plaster wall, one baseboard line, the distant closed door, the bed. FRAMING, AND THIS PARAGRAPH WINS OVER ANYTHING ABOVE ABOUT HOW MUCH ROOM IS IN FRAME: the camera is close. The top of the handler's head sits one quarter of the way down the picture — not lower — and she and Lucy together fill the middle half of the frame from top to bottom, so that they are large, not small figures in a large room. Empty wall above their heads is one band, not half the picture. To get them this large, the door may be cut by the left edge of the frame; that is fine. Do not draw the whole wall; do not pull the camera back to show the span of floor.
mustBeTrue: the handler is crouched down on her heels with her head low beside Lucy's rather than standing or bending from the waist, both of them are well back from the closed door with clear floor between, no treat appears anywhere, the bed is on the RIGHT of the frame with the door on the LEFT, and the top of the handler's head sits about a quarter of the way down the frame with a clear band of empty wall above both heads, nothing that matters falling in the top fifth, the bottom quarter or the outer eighth of either side.
